title: Why does the Vyra API return FOOTAGE_TOO_LONG?
reader: Developer resolving the documented input-duration refusal
job: The Vyra API documents a three-hour total video-footage limit per video request. FOOTAGE_TOO_LONG means the supplied videos exceed that total. The current docs say this is detected before analysis or editing, with nothing charged.
source: Official API footage, limits and errors
nextAction: Review the suggested edit against your footage and use the native app or current API docs

title: Why does the Vyra API say FILE_EXPIRED?
reader: Developer recovering from documented source-file expiry
job: Vyra’s current API docs say an uploaded file is kept for seven days after its last use. FILE_EXPIRED means its source video has been removed after that period without use. Request a new upload link and send the source again.
source: Official API reusable footage and expiry documentation

title: Should I use speech captions or a label in my iPhone video?
reader: Creator choosing between transcribed speech and explanatory text
job: Use speech captions when the viewer needs the spoken words. Use a short text label for context the recording does not say, such as a step name or a date. In Vyra on iPhone, Captions and Text are separate tools.
